titles: Statement of Work: Warehouse System Implementation
openings: This Statement of Work is issued under the Master Services Agreement between {{first}} (the "Supplier") and {{second}} (the "Customer"), and incorporates its terms.

This Statement of Work describes one project: the Supplier will implement its warehouse management system at the Customer's distribution centre. It sets out the scope, the deliverables, the timetable, the fees and the responsibilities of each party for that project only.

{{secondShort}} (the "Customer") engages {{firstShort}} (the "Supplier") to carry out the project described below, on the terms of the master services agreement already in force between {{second}} and {{first}}.

This document is a statement of work under that agreement. It orders the implementation of the Supplier's warehouse management system at the Customer's distribution centre, and records the work, deliverables, milestones and fees for that project.

sections.heading: Scope of Work
variants: The Supplier shall configure its warehouse management system for the Customer's distribution centre, integrate it with the Customer's order management system, migrate the Customer's current stock records into it, and train the Customer's staff to use it.
Hardware, network changes at the distribution centre, and changes to the Customer's order management system are outside the scope of this Statement of Work.

The project covers the design, configuration, testing and go-live of the warehouse management system for the distribution centre, including an interface to the Customer's order management system and the transfer of existing stock records.
The Supplier is not responsible for buying or installing scanners, printers or other hardware, which the Customer shall provide.

sections.heading: Deliverables
variants: The Supplier shall deliver: a design specification describing the configuration and the interface; the configured system, tested and ready for go-live; and a training and handover pack, with two days of on-site training for up to twelve of the Customer's staff.

The deliverables are the design specification, which records how the system will be configured and how the interface will work; the configured and tested system; and the training and handover pack, including on-site training for the Customer's warehouse supervisors.

sections.heading: Timetable and Milestones
variants: The project has three milestones. Milestone 1 is delivery of the design specification, four weeks after the start date. Milestone 2 is delivery of the configured system for testing, twelve weeks after the start date. Milestone 3 is go-live and delivery of the training and handover pack, sixteen weeks after the start date.
The start date is the first working day after both parties sign this Statement of Work.

Work starts on the first working day after this Statement of Work is signed. The Supplier shall deliver the design specification by the end of week four (Milestone 1), the configured system for testing by the end of week twelve (Milestone 2), and go-live with the training and handover pack by the end of week sixteen (Milestone 3).

sections.heading: Acceptance
variants: The Customer shall review each deliverable within ten working days of receiving it, and either accept it in writing or list the ways in which it fails to meet this Statement of Work. The Supplier shall correct any listed failure and resubmit the deliverable for review. A milestone is achieved when the Customer accepts its deliverable.

Each deliverable is accepted when the Customer signs an acceptance certificate for it, or ten working days after delivery if the Customer has not by then notified any material defect. The Supplier shall fix any notified defect promptly, and the same acceptance process then applies again.

sections.heading: Fees and Payment
variants: The fixed price for this project is £186,000, excluding VAT, paid in three instalments: £37,200 on acceptance of Milestone 1, £93,000 on acceptance of Milestone 2, and the final instalment of £55,800 on acceptance of Milestone 3.
The Supplier shall invoice each instalment when its milestone is accepted, and the Customer shall pay each invoice within thirty days of receipt.

The Supplier shall charge for this project on a time and materials basis at £1,150 per consultant day, excluding VAT, up to a ceiling of £190,000. The Supplier shall not exceed the ceiling without the Customer's written approval.
The Supplier shall invoice monthly in arrears, with a timesheet for each consultant, and the Customer shall pay each invoice within thirty days of receipt.

sections.heading: Customer Responsibilities
variants: The Customer shall give the Supplier's consultants access to the distribution centre during working hours, provide test data and a test environment for its order management system, and make its warehouse supervisors available for workshops and training. The Supplier is not responsible for any delay caused by the Customer's failure to do so.

The Customer shall name a project lead with authority to make decisions, provide an extract of its current stock records in the agreed format by the end of week six, and make the scanners and printers available at the distribution centre before testing starts.

sections.heading: Project Governance
variants: Each party shall appoint a project manager. The project managers shall meet weekly to review progress against the milestones, record risks and agree actions, and the Supplier shall circulate a short written report after each meeting.

The Supplier's project manager shall send the Customer's project lead a progress report every two weeks, covering work done, the status of each milestone, open risks and the days used. Either side may call a meeting on two days' notice to deal with a problem.

sections.heading: Changes and Term
variants: Any change to the scope, deliverables, timetable or fees of this Statement of Work must be agreed in a written change note signed by both parties. This Statement of Work ends when the Customer accepts Milestone 3, unless it is terminated earlier under the master services agreement.

Either party may propose a change to this project in writing; the Supplier shall state its effect on the timetable and fees, and no change applies until both parties sign it. This Statement of Work expires on completion of the project, and its terms otherwise follow the master services agreement.
